meta.subtitle: Q3 FY26 10-Q: custom AI accelerators lift revenue 86%, while a lease Backstop and customer concentration raise the stakes

analystCommentary:
Broadcom earns a BUY, though only narrowly. The call turns on how much weight the downside deserves rather than on any doubt about the quarter.

The fiscal third quarter confirmed that custom AI accelerators and AI networking now drive the company. What changed is the shape of the risk. A handful of buyers take most of the AI output, those buyers need outside capital to deploy it, and Broadcom has begun to guarantee part of one customer's lease obligations to close that gap.

The shares sit well below their 52-week high of $495.00, and no source in hand explains the decline. On consensus estimates for fiscal 2027 the price asks for less than the Street's numbers imply, which is why the weighted outcome clears the BUY bar. A heavier downside weight would not clear it. The valuation section sets out that argument, and the final recommendation states what would change the call.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Broadcom Inc. designs, develops and supplies semiconductor devices and infrastructure software. The 10-Q reports two segments. Semiconductor solutions covers custom AI accelerators (which the company calls XPUs), Ethernet switching and routing, wireless and broadband devices, storage connectivity and IP licensing. Infrastructure software covers private cloud software including VMware Cloud Foundation, mainframe, cybersecurity and enterprise software, plus the FC SAN business.

The company was founded in 1961 and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Its fiscal year ends in early November, and fiscal 2025 revenue was $63.9B. The vendor data shows a single consolidated line for fiscal 2025, so this report takes the segment split from the 10-Q.

thesis.body:
The third quarter of fiscal 2026, ended August 2, 2026, showed the AI ramp arriving in the income statement. Revenue reached $29.6B, up 86% year over year. The CEO put AI semiconductor revenue at $16.7 billion, up 221% year over year and 54% quarter over quarter, and guided the fourth quarter higher again.

The cost of that growth is concentration and a new funding structure: a few customers buy most of the AI output, and Broadcom now guarantees part of a customer's lease payments so that deployments can be financed. Both are argued under Risks.

At $355.14 the shares already discount part of that risk. We rate them BUY with a $380–$470 range, a close call that the valuation section explains.

catalysts: Fiscal fourth-quarter results, set against the revenue and AI guidance the company gave on September 2, 2026 (see Growth).
The fiscal 2026 10-K, which will update the customer-concentration and Backstop disclosures.
New AI XPV tranches with outside financial partners, each of which would widen the funded pipeline the platform is meant to build.
Infrastructure software renewals, whose timing the 10-Q says moves that segment's revenue from period to period.
risks: A pause by any of the top five end customers, which the company says could have a material adverse effect (see Risks).
The lease Backstop under the AI XPV platform, a contingent liability that grows as racks are deployed.
Tighter credit, which the 10-Q warns could limit customers' ability to finance their AI capital spending.
A wide gap between GAAP and non-GAAP earnings, which makes the adjusted multiples look cheaper (see Valuation).

financials.incomeCommentary:
Annual revenue more than doubled between FY21 and FY25, reaching $63.9B, but the path was uneven. Growth slowed to +7.9% in FY23 and jumped to +44.0% in FY24. Operating margin fell to 26.1% in FY24 and recovered to 39.9% in FY25; the sources in hand do not break down the FY24 dip.

The fiscal third quarter shows real operating leverage. GAAP operating income was $15,955 million against $5,887 million in the prior-year quarter, while total operating expenses fell to $4,501 million from $4,816 million as research and development and SG&A both declined. GAAP operating margin reached 54%, up from 37%.

Two items temper the read. Cost of products sold rose to 24% of net revenue from 19%, as products, which carry the hardware costs, grew to 82% of revenue from 70%. Products revenue also included $3,465 million of upfront license revenue with immaterial related costs, against $1,916 million reclassified into the prior-year quarter, so part of the products growth is licensing rather than hardware. The provision for income taxes rose to $2,187 million from $1,145 million, which the excerpt does not explain.

GAAP diluted EPS was $2.68 against $0.85 a year earlier. We read the margin step-up as mostly genuine leverage on a flat cost base, with license timing adding quarter-to-quarter noise.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Liquidity looks ample. Cash and cash equivalents were $24.0 billion at the end of the fiscal third quarter, up from $19.6 billion a quarter earlier, and the TTM current ratio is 2.50 against 1.71 at FY25 year-end.

The vendor's debt lines need care. They show FY25 total debt of $3.2B and a net cash position, yet the quarter carried interest expense of $778 million, the 10-Q lists "substantial indebtedness" among its risk factors, and the company repurchased $5,641 million of its senior notes in the quarter. Those disclosures do not fit a nearly debt-free balance sheet, so we do not rely on the vendor's net-debt figure and make no net-cash claim. TTM interest coverage of 13.7x says the debt is comfortably serviced either way.

The item that matters more sits off the balance sheet: the AI XPV Backstop, a contingent liability whose fair value the company says was not material. Its mechanics and size are argued under Risks. Our view of the balance sheet is that it can absorb a slowdown, but not one that also triggers the Backstop.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash generation is the strongest part of the record. Operating cash flow rose every year from FY21 to FY25, reaching $27.5B, while capital expenditure stayed small. FY25 free cash flow was $26.9B, a 42.1% margin, below the 49.2% of FY23. In the fiscal third quarter, free cash flow was $13.7 billion, or 46 percent of revenue, per the earnings release.

Shareholder returns lean on the dividend. FY25 dividends paid were $11.1B against share repurchases of $2.5B, down from $7.2B in FY24.

Stock-based compensation was $2,019 million in the quarter. Free cash flow does not deduct it and non-GAAP earnings exclude it, so both measures leave out a real cost to owners that is paid in shares rather than cash.

The TTM free cash flow yield of 2.3% is low, a reminder that the price assumes much larger cash flows ahead. The capital-light model means most of the revenue ramp should reach free cash flow, which is the core of the bull argument.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
Trailing and forward multiples sit far apart because earnings are ramping. The 45.3x TTM P/E is on GAAP earnings for the twelve months through August 2, 2026, a window that includes quarters before the ramp: GAAP diluted EPS was $1.91 in the fiscal second quarter against $2.68 in the third. EV/EBITDA of 33.1x and P/S of 19.0x are also trailing measures.

The vendor's "NTM" P/E of 30.5x lines up with FY26E consensus EPS of $11.66, so it is in effect a current-year multiple, and fiscal 2026 ends on November 1, 2026. The forward frame that matters is FY27E consensus EPS of $19.39, on which the shares trade at ~18.3x.

The consensus EPS basis is not stated, and GAAP and non-GAAP diverge widely. Third-quarter non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.32, and the release's adjusted measures exclude amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, stock-based compensation and restructuring, among other items. GAAP diluted EPS for the three fiscal quarters was $6.09, and the fourth quarter would have to be far above the third to reach the FY26E figure on that basis. The consensus is therefore probably on an adjusted basis, and the forward multiples would be higher on GAAP earnings.

The Street is close to unanimous: 47 Buy and 3 Hold ratings, a median target of $535.00, and a range from $215.88 to $715.00. No peer multiples are available, so we cannot say whether the forward multiple is cheap against the group, only that it is low against Broadcom's own growth.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: AI XPV tranches beyond the initial one close on schedule, AI semiconductor growth continues past the fourth-quarter guide, and fiscal 2027 earnings beat consensus. Concentration stays high but no customer pauses. The market pays a multiple in the mid-twenties on FY27E EPS, which puts the shares near the $531.31 consensus target.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The fourth quarter lands near guidance and fiscal 2027 EPS arrives close to the consensus discussed above. Concentration and the Backstop stay as they are, without incident. As the market's frame rolls toward fiscal 2028, it pays a multiple in the low twenties on FY27E EPS, above today's forward multiple but well below the current-year one.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: AI deployments slow: a top-five customer defers racks, or a later AI XPV tranche fails to find financing, and fiscal 2027 EPS lands about a quarter below consensus. The market keeps roughly today's forward multiple on the lower figure, which puts the shares below the $289.96 52-week low. No payment under the Backstop is needed for this case; the market only has to start pricing one.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The horizon is twelve months. Weights of 25% Bull, 50% Base and 25% Bear give a weighted fair value of $408.75, expected upside of +15.1%, bear-case downside of 25.4% and reward/risk of 0.59x. The rule derives BUY and we take it, but the margin is thin.

Base carries half the weight because the near-term evidence is strong. The company guided the fourth quarter higher, and the forward multiple already sits well below the trailing ones. Base needs no beat, only for consensus to hold and for a modest re-rating as the market looks toward fiscal 2028. Bull at a quarter of the weight sits near the Street's own target, which we do not treat as the central case.

The deciding split is Base against Bear, and it can be argued both ways. For a heavier Bear: the shares trade at $355.14, far below the 52-week high, after a quarter in which revenue, operating income and free cash flow all rose sharply year over year, which suggests the market is already pricing something the sources do not name. The daily closes since late August move within a narrow band, so the fall from the high predates the third-quarter release, and that strong release did not lift the shares. The funding structure, with Broadcom guaranteeing part of a customer's lease, is also new and untested. For keeping Bear at a quarter: the Bear already assumes a sizeable estimate cut, the Backstop's fair value was not material, no amounts have been paid, and nothing in the 10-Q shows demand weakening.

Moving a modest amount of weight from Base to Bear would derive HOLD, so the call is close. We keep the weights because they are what we believe today. The $380–$470 range brackets Base and sits above the current price.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The 10-Q reports two segments, and the fiscal third quarter shows how far the mix has moved. Semiconductor solutions revenue was $20,839 million, up 127% from the prior-year quarter, and made up 70% of net revenue against 57% a year earlier. The 10-Q credits "strong demand for our networking solutions, primarily custom AI accelerators and AI networking products." Infrastructure software revenue was $8,752 million, up 29%, though only 13% for the three fiscal quarters, and the 10-Q says the timing and extent of renewals cause variations from period to period. Broadcom is now primarily an AI semiconductor supplier with a large software business alongside it, and the software side is the steadier of the two.

moatFactors.name: Custom accelerator design relationships
moatFactors.body: AI semiconductor revenue was $20.2 billion in fiscal 2025, up 65% from $12.2 billion, per the proxy, and the AI XPV platform is meant to enable more than 20 gigawatts of capacity on the company's custom XPUs through 2028. A design built for one customer's systems ties both sides to the program, which is the source of the advantage. The sources give no data on how easily a customer could switch, so we credit the advantage with protecting volume more reliably than price.

moatFactors.name: Infrastructure software base
moatFactors.body: Infrastructure software revenue rose 26% to $27.0 billion in fiscal 2025, which the proxy attributes to "strong adoption of VMware Cloud Foundation." The 10-Q refers to customer contracts without the right to terminate, which give part of the revenue contractual weight. The risk factors also say software growth depends on demand for the data center virtualization portfolio and on customer acceptance of the company's strategy, so this advantage rests on adoption continuing.

moatFactors.name: Profitability through the cycle
moatFactors.body: Gross margin stayed between 61.4% and 68.9% from FY21 to FY25, and FCF margin did not fall below 37.6%. That record held through a slow-growth year and a year of operating-margin compression, which suggests pricing power that is structural rather than borrowed from the cycle.

moatFactors.name: Customer bargaining power
moatFactors.body: The concentration set out under Risks gives a few buyers the weight to press on price and terms. The Backstop shows the company now supports a customer's financing to secure deployments, which is a cost of winning the business rather than a sign of pricing power.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The returns look like those of a WIDE-moat business: stable gross margins, capital-light cash conversion and a growing share of revenue from custom designs. What holds us back is who captures the value over time. A handful of customers buy most of the AI output, they need outside capital to deploy it, and Broadcom has begun to guarantee part of that capital. A supplier with a fully durable advantage should not need to share its customers' credit risk. The software base is the more defensible half, but it is now the smaller one. The rating will move with the breadth of the AI customer base rather than with margins.

points: Fourth-quarter guidance, dated September 2, 2026, calls for revenue of approximately $34.8 billion, up 93% from the prior-year period, and the CEO expects AI semiconductor revenue of $21.7 billion, up 236% year over year. The company cautions that actual results will vary and "the variations may be material."

Consensus has FY26E revenue of ~$106B (+66%) and FY27E revenue of $173.9B, so the Street expects the ramp to run through fiscal 2027. The FY27E figure sits well above four quarters at the guided fourth-quarter level, so it needs further sequential growth from deployments that the 10-Q says are lumpy: fluctuations "may be magnified by the timing of customer deployments."

The AI XPV platform is meant to enable more than 20 gigawatts of compute through 2028. Its first tranche, launched in June 2026, is $35 billion for more than 1 gigawatt for one customer. The platform could turn demand into funded orders, but each tranche depends on financial partners whose appetite the risk factors tie to credit conditions.

Margin is guided flat. The CFO expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP operating margin of 66%, "flat from a year ago," so earnings growth from here should track revenue rather than margin expansion. The shift toward products and their higher cost of sales (see Financials) is why we assume no margin upside.

Infrastructure software adds a slower second engine. The proxy ties fiscal 2025 software growth to adoption of VMware Cloud Foundation, and the third quarter grew faster than the year-to-date pace, but renewal timing makes that quarter a poor run rate.

management.leadership: Hock E. Tan is President and CEO and, per the proxy statement filed March 2, 2026, is not deemed an independent director. That proxy named four executive officers for fiscal 2025: Mr. Tan; Kirsten M. Spears, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Accounting Officer; Mark D. Brazeal, Chief Legal and Corporate Affairs Officer; and Charlie B. Kawwas, Ph.D., President, Semiconductor Solutions Group. The September 2, 2026 earnings release quotes Amie Thuener as CFO, so the finance role has changed hands since that proxy; the sources in hand do not say when or why. The quarter's execution, with revenue up sharply while operating expenses fell, reflects well on the team, and the CFO change during a large new financing program is a point to note rather than a concern.
management.capitalAllocation: The quarter's highlights list $3,103 million of cash dividends and $5,641 million of senior notes repurchased, so cash went to the dividend and to retiring debt. The quarterly dividend of $0.65 per share was raised 10% in fiscal Q1 2026, per the proxy, which also says the company returned $13.6 billion to stockholders in fiscal 2025. The quarter's free cash flow covered the dividend several times over. The new use of the balance sheet is the AI XPV Backstop, which commits Broadcom's credit rather than its cash to customers' deployments. Paying down notes while taking on a contingent commitment of that size is, in our view, the right order.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement filed March 2, 2026, seven of eight director nominees are independent under Nasdaq standards. The Chairman, Dr. Samueli, is independent, and the CEO and Chairman roles are held by different people. Eddy W. Hartenstein, the Lead Independent Director, was not standing for re-election; the board's stated structure calls for a Lead Independent Director only when the Chairman is not independent. The Audit Committee must review and approve related party transactions. More than 90% of executive officers' total compensation is variable, built on multi-year performance-based equity awards; the proxy's claims of outperformance are the company's own. We see a conventional, independent board with pay tied to long-dated equity goals, and nothing in the excerpt raises a governance concern.
management.insiderOwnership: As of February 24, 2026, per the proxy, all current directors and executive officers as a group beneficially owned 89,467,014 shares, or 1.9% of common stock. Most of that is the 85,559,569 shares (1.8%) attributed to Dr. Samueli; the excerpt cuts off the footnote that explains how they are held. Mr. Tan held 908,474 shares, under 1%. The five-percent holders listed were The Vanguard Group at 9.9% and BlackRock, Inc. at 7.3%, based on Schedule 13G/A filings dated October 4, 2024 and January 26, 2024, so those figures are stale. No holder is near control. Outside shareholders rely on the board's independence rather than on a large anchor owner, and the CEO's alignment runs mainly through performance equity rather than through a large stake.

idiosyncratic: Customer concentration. Direct sales to one semiconductor customer, a distributor, were 50% of net revenue in the fiscal third quarter against 32% a year earlier, and the company believes its top five end customers were approximately 55%, up from approximately 40%. A pause or redesign at one buyer removes a visible share of revenue, and the 10-Q says losing any top-five customer "could have a material adverse effect." The fiscal 2026 10-K will show whether the distributor and top-five shares rose further.

The AI XPV Backstop. Broadcom backs a customer's lease obligations to a financial partner over the 5-year lease terms. On a default, its liability equals any gap between 85% of the outstanding amounts owed and what the racks fetch on sale, with a maximum potential liability of approximately $29 billion once all racks are deployed. The company believes such guarantees have a low probability of being called, and the fair value was not material. The risk is correlated: a default would likely come when AI hardware values are also falling. Note 10 of each filing is where any payment or new guarantee would show.

Customer funding. The company says deploying AI infrastructure "requires our customers to access significant capital," and the risk factors warn that tight credit markets could adversely affect customers' ability to obtain financing for their capital spending. If financing dries up, orders slip even when end demand holds. The pace of new AI XPV tranches after the initial one is the clearest signal.

Earnings quality and timing. GAAP operating income of $16.0 billion compares with non-GAAP operating income of $20.1 billion, and the adjusted figure excludes stock-based compensation. The 10-Q also warns that large orders or delays can cause quarterly revenue to "fluctuate significantly," and upfront license revenue varies by quarter. A widening gap between the two operating income measures would be the sign to discount adjusted earnings further.
risks.systemic: Broadcom operates in a cyclical industry that its own 10-Q describes as "undergoing profound change due to AI." The risk factors also cite trade tensions and related tariffs, governmental regulations and trade restrictions, and dependence on a limited number of contract manufacturers and suppliers. A broad pull-back in AI capital spending would hit the semiconductor side directly and the AI XPV financing partners at the same time, which is why the downside cases cluster. Higher rates or tighter credit would raise the cost of the financing the platform depends on. Credit conditions for AI infrastructure and any new trade restrictions are the macro variables that matter most here.

body: BUY, with a $380–$470 target range over twelve months. The quarter proved the AI ramp, and the shares price less than consensus implies. The call is close, because it depends on a downside weight that a reasonable reader could set higher, as the valuation section explains.

We would move to HOLD if fourth-quarter revenue falls short of the approximately $34.8 billion guidance, if any amount is paid under the Backstop, or if the fiscal 2026 10-K shows the top-five customer share rising further while fiscal 2027 consensus EPS is cut. We would consider STRONG BUY if a later AI XPV tranche brings in a different customer and the 10-K shows the top-five share falling while margins hold.
